scope: Warm synthetic FP32 operators and one transformer block, not pretrained full-stage timing

sparse_geometry_source.features: Random FP32 features on a prefix of frozen decoded geometry; not a full decoder benchmark

selection_notes: The fastest tested positive transformer-block combination used full-query cross attention, self query chunk 1024, and FFN rows 8192.
FFN and cross-attention-only differences were small; synthetic timing is not a production speedup guarantee.
The sparse test used random 64-channel features on the first 262144 coordinates of a frozen decoded asset, not the whole decoder.
The math backend used more temporary VRAM and was slower, so production keeps PyTorch automatic SDPA dispatch.
All case inputs coexist in the microbenchmark; incremental peak allocation is not a full-pipeline VRAM forecast.
Profiler captures were separate from timing; raw Chrome traces remain private in the jobs Volume and local outputs.
